get.description: Liveness — the process is up.
Readiness — the database is reachable.

Who the caller is, and whether this deployment requires a key at all.

A cheap probe for the UI's connection state: it touches no sidecar, unlike
``/capabilities``. It is also the one place a browser can learn that the
API is open (``auth_required`` false) — worth saying out loud in the UI,
because an open scanner is an unauthenticated active-scan endpoint.

schema.title: Response Auth Status Auth Status Get

get.description:
What this deployment can run, and what this tenant may run.

``passes`` answers for the deployment and is cached briefly — the probes are
network calls to sidecars. ``premium`` answers for the calling tenant and is
never cached per tenant, so a plan change lands on the next request.

post.description:
Ask for an account. The answer is the same whether or not the email is
already registered, so the endpoint cannot be used to list accounts.

Every request counts against the caller's address, accepted or not, and
is counted before the password is hashed: scrypt is the expensive part.

Sign in. Failures count per email and per client address; a locked
bucket answers 429 before the password is checked, so a correct guess
during a lockout is indistinguishable from a wrong one.
End the presented session. An API token is not revoked by this.
Dev only: the bundled target with its live spec and both seed identities, not run.

patch.description: Edit the scan's target base URL. Rejected while a scan is active.

delete.description: Delete a scan and all of its data. Refused while a scan is active.

schema.title: Response Delete Scan Scans  Scan Id  Delete

put.description: Save the request cadence used by manual and scheduled runs.

Record which settings a project file (aidetector.yml) owns.

Metadata only: it changes nothing a run does, so it is accepted while a scan
runs and needs no authorization. The web reads it to mark those settings
read-only.

delete.description: Hand every setting back to the web.

get.description:
The fields a running scan changes, without its collections.

The web polls this every second while a scan is active; ``GET /scans/{id}``
remains the full detail read.

patch.description: Bulk enable/disable operations so the UI can exclude endpoints from a run.

get.description: How this scan's spec says its API authenticates — the credential form's defaults.

schema.title: Response Delete Credential Scans  Scan Id  Credentials  Cred Id  Delete

get.description:
Whether running this scan needs proof the workspace owns its target.

Answers the run gate's ownership question ahead of the run, so the panel can
say "verify this domain first" instead of the run being refused. Nothing is
fetched from the target; the run still proves ownership live.

post.description: Queue the scan as a background job. Poll the scan / events for progress.

Cooperatively cancel a running scan; the runner stops between checks.

Deliberately not EditableScanDep — cancelling is the one write that *needs*
the scan to be running.

get.description:
The latest events, returned oldest-first for the activity log.

The detail read no longer ships every event the scan ever emitted; a
long-running scan's log is bounded by ``limit``.

schema.title: Response List Events Scans  Scan Id  Events Get

get.description:
Run history, newest first — re-runs replace live findings, not history.

``trace_count`` is computed in SQL; the run's full trace JSONB is not
loaded just to count it.

schema.title: Response List Runs Scans  Scan Id  Runs Get

get.description: One page of a run's request/response trace, sliced in SQL.

What changed between two runs — new, fixed, still there.

Defaults to the two most recent runs, which is the question people actually
ask ("what changed since last time"). Needs two runs: a scan with one has
nothing to compare against, and saying so beats reporting every finding as
new.

Per-endpoint activity for the latest run: requests, checks, findings.

Empty until the scan has finished a run. Shows every operation, so a row with
``requests: 0`` means the endpoint was in scope but no check exercised it (or
it was excluded — see ``enabled``).

schema.title: Response Get Coverage Scans  Scan Id  Coverage Get

get.description:
Filtered findings, ordered server-side so a page is a true slice.

The list used to arrive whole and be filtered in the browser; at scale a
page of the wrong rows is worse than useless, so the filters and ordering
are part of the query. The response stays a bare list for existing clients.

parameters.name: endpoint

parameters.description: An endpoint label as the UI shows it (`GET /users/{id}`); matches findings with an operation and evidence-only findings alike.

schema.title: Response List Findings Scans  Scan Id  Findings Get

get.description: Counts over every finding, not just the page the list happens to show.

patch.description:
Mark a finding confirmed or dismissed (false positive).

The verdict is remembered against the finding's fingerprint as well as its
row, so the next run does not hand back a false positive somebody already
dismissed.

get.description:
Every live finding with an assignment or a discussion.

A discussion is independent of an assignment: a comment written before
anyone is assigned (or after the assignment is cleared) still has to be
readable, so a commented fingerprint with no work row is returned as an
unassigned, "open" item. Otherwise the UI would accept a comment and then
lose it on the next read.

schema.title: Response List Finding Work Scans  Scan Id  Work Get

put.description:
Create or partially update the work item for one live finding.

An omitted field is unchanged; an explicit null clears owner/due date.

delete.description: Remove a work item. Its comments are separate rows and stay.

schema.title: Response Delete Finding Work Scans  Scan Id  Findings  Fingerprint  Work Delete

post.description: Comment on a live finding, attributed to the acting person.

delete.description: Delete a comment that belongs to this scan.

schema.title: Response Delete Finding Comment Scans  Scan Id  Comments  Comment Id  Delete

get.description: Findings as a SARIF 2.1.0 document, for CI security dashboards.
Per-call token ledger and total cost for the scan.
Download the full scan result as JSON.
Download a formatted PDF report of the scan's findings.
Standalone HTML report — renders in the browser, printable to PDF.

Pentest-grade Markdown report — a premium deliverable.

Gated like ``POST /scans/{id}/ask``; the PDF/HTML/JSON exports stay
available on every plan.

post.description:
Answer a natural-language question about the scan's findings (premium).

Takes the editable guard: answering writes token-ledger rows, so it must not
run while a worker is still writing to the scan.

put.description:
Enable or clear a recurring schedule (re-run every N minutes).

Enabling one starts active scans nobody will click "run" for, so it answers
the same authorization and entitlement gates as a manual run, and saves the
options every scheduled run will use. Clearing needs no authorization.

post.description: Suggest identity setup (public, one key, or roles) from a spec's security.

put.description:
Set the workspace's AI spend and run-admission limits.

Omitted fields stay unchanged; an explicit null removes that limit.

Run both proofs now and record the result. A failed check is a 200 with

schema.title: Response Ops Status Ops Status Get

post.description: Claim a scan to run on the CLI machine. Mirrors the run endpoint's gates.
Append progress events and stamp liveness; returns the cancel flag.
Stamp liveness and learn whether a cancel was requested from the web.

The AI pre-scan plan for a local run: the claim's operations, riskiest first.

Only a run that claimed ``plan`` may ask — the options archived at claim are
what was authorized and priced. Asking again returns the stored plan rather
than spending twice. Every AI failure is a ``plan_skipped`` event and the
spec order, exactly as on a server run.

get.description:
Recall what prior heavy runs found on this target, for this tenant.

Token-scoped like every other runner call, so the runner reaches only the
memory of the scan it is executing. Episodic memory steers the agent; it is
never authoritative — a recalled weakness still has to be re-confirmed, and
the engine grades whatever the agent produces.

post.description:
Run one planner call for a local run, priced here, capped per run.

Only a run that asked for an in-loop AI pass may call, and only for a known
mode. Every failure degrades to an empty result so the runner falls back to
its deterministic path — an AI problem never fails a local run.
Validate and persist an uploaded result bundle, then finish the run.
Mark the run failed (the runner crashed or could not finish).

AgentMemoryRow.title: AgentMemoryRow
AgentMemoryRow.description: One recalled prior finding for the heavy-lane agent.

AiModelUsage.title: AiModelUsage
AiModelUsage.description: One model the scan used, aggregated across its calls.

AuthHintsOut.title: AuthHintsOut
AuthHintsOut.description:
How the spec says its API authenticates — defaults for the setup forms.

Advisory only: nothing here reaches the engine.

AuthHintsRequest.title: AuthHintsRequest
AuthHintsRequest.description: A spec to read auth hints from, before any scan exists (``aidetector init``).

AuthSchemeHintOut.title: AuthSchemeHintOut
AuthSchemeHintOut.description: One ``securitySchemes`` entry, translated into credential-form terms.

Confidence.title: Confidence
Confidence.description:
How strongly a finding's evidence supports the claim the finding makes.

The evidence-tier vocabulary the product already uses in prose — the
coverage page, the landing page and every check docstring — promoted to
data, so consumers can act on it rather than re-read it: SARIF levels,
report grouping, and a CI gate that blocks a build on verified findings
only. Severity says *how bad if real*; confidence says *how sure we are*.

``heuristic`` is the deliberate default everywhere. A site that forgets to
grade itself understates its own evidence, which is the safe direction for
a scanner: it never promotes a lead to a confirmation by omission.

ConfigSource.title: ConfigSource
ConfigSource.description:
Where a run's settings came from when a project file supplied them.

``digest`` is the SHA-256 of the file's bytes, so two runs from an unchanged
file compare equal however many commits sit between them; ``commit`` is
there for a person reading the run, not for the comparison.

CoverageRow.title: CoverageRow
CoverageRow.description: What the engine did to one operation during a run.

CredentialOut.title: CredentialOut
CredentialOut.description: Note: no secret field — credentials are write-only.

DomainProofOut.title: DomainProofOut
DomainProofOut.description: One proof's outcome from the last explicit check.

FindingCounts.title: FindingCounts
FindingCounts.description: Live findings per severity. Dismissed false positives are not counted.

premium.title: Premium
premium.description:
Whether the check that produced this finding is a premium-tier check.

Read from the registry (not stored on the row), so the label always
tracks the check's own ``premium`` trait — the single source of truth.

FindingSummaryOut.title: FindingSummaryOut
FindingSummaryOut.description:
Full-result counts for the attention summary.

The findings list is paged, so a count derived from the first page would be
wrong for every scan larger than a page. These numbers come from grouped
queries over all of the scan's findings.

FindingWorkIn.title: FindingWorkIn
FindingWorkIn.description:
A partial work-item update.

An omitted key is unchanged; an explicit ``null`` clears ``owner`` or
``due_date``. ``status`` null is treated as omitted.

GrantType.title: GrantType
GrantType.description:
How a credential obtains the token it authenticates with.

``static`` is the original behaviour: the stored secret *is* the token/value
sent on every request. The others mint a fresh token at scan time by calling
the target's own auth endpoint, so a scan (especially a scheduled one) never
carries a token that has since expired — and the scanner can test an API
whose tokens are short-lived by design.

LocalRunConfig.title: LocalRunConfig
LocalRunConfig.description: Claim response: the per-run token (returned once) and the run config.

ManagedConfigIn.title: ManagedConfigIn
ManagedConfigIn.description: What the CLI reports a project file owns on this scan.

MutationRequestRow.title: MutationRequestRow
MutationRequestRow.description:
Sanitized request metadata for one trace.

``json_body`` is the redacted payload the scanner sent. It is retained where
a response body is only sampled, because it is data we generated rather than
the target's — and reading it beside the response is what answers "why was
this rejected".

MutationResponseRow.title: MutationResponseRow
MutationResponseRow.description:
Sanitized response metadata for one request trace.

``body`` is the redacted, truncated response text — enough to read why a
write was accepted or rejected, but with secrets/PII masked and cut at the
trace limit so a scan cannot accumulate target data. It is empty when
``body_omitted``: the response was not text, or the run had already spent
its body budget. ``truncated`` means the retained text was cut short.

MutationRow.title: MutationRow
MutationRow.description:
One request/response trace (read and write).

Values are redacted, not absent: both bodies are masked by known secret,
sensitive field name and PII shape before they are stored. ``identity`` is
the credential whose headers went out — the fact a reviewer needs to read an
authorization finding, and the one the redacted Authorization header hides.
``pass_`` says which pass made the call (``engine`` or ``discovery``); it is
serialized as ``pass``, which is a Python keyword.

OastConfig.title: OastConfig
OastConfig.description:
The out-of-band collector the runner registers with, when the service has one.

The token is the collector's, handed to the CLI user for this run; the
runner masks it in everything it uploads.

OperationSelection.title: OperationSelection
OperationSelection.description: One entry in a bulk enable/disable request.

OperationsUpdate.title: OperationsUpdate
OperationsUpdate.description: Bulk-set which operations are in scope for the run.

PlanRow.title: PlanRow
PlanRow.description: The AI planner's risk priority for one operation.

ResourceAttemptRow.title: ResourceAttemptRow
ResourceAttemptRow.description: One bounded resource-create attempt, without its request values.

ResourceRow.title: ResourceRow
ResourceRow.description: One resource the mutation-gated setup pass created, sanitized.

RunDiffOut.title: RunDiffOut
RunDiffOut.description: What changed between two runs of one scan.

RunGaps.title: RunGaps
RunGaps.description:
What a run was asked to do and did not.

``not_run`` names requested adjunct tools that never ran; ``budget_exhausted``
says the request cap refused later requests. The diff counts findings those
gaps could have hidden as not re-tested, never as fixed.

authorized.title: Authorized
authorized.description: I own or am authorized to security-test this target.

RunTraceOut.title: RunTraceOut
RunTraceOut.description: One page of a run's request trace.

RunnerAiIn.title: RunnerAiIn
RunnerAiIn.description:
A local run asking the service to run one planner call on its behalf.

The runner sends no secrets and no raw bodies — ``payload`` is the already
redacted, evidence-shaped input the planner mode expects. The service runs
the planner, prices it on the run's ledger, and enforces the per-run cap.

RunnerAiOut.title: RunnerAiOut
RunnerAiOut.description:
The planner's structured result, or an empty one when it was unavailable
or the per-run AI budget is spent — the runner degrades either way.

RunnerFinding.title: RunnerFinding
RunnerFinding.description:
One finding a runner uploads. The server re-derives identity, remediation
and references, so those are not accepted here.

RunnerMemoryOut.title: RunnerMemoryOut
RunnerMemoryOut.description: What prior heavy runs found on this target, for this tenant.

RunnerPlanOut.title: RunnerPlanOut
RunnerPlanOut.description:
The run's operations in AI priority order, and what the plan step said.

The events are the runner's to journal, so a local run's event stream
reads the same as a server run's.

RunnerTraceRequest.title: RunnerTraceRequest
RunnerTraceRequest.description: What the runner sent: header names with redacted values, field names, our payload.

RunnerTraceResponse.title: RunnerTraceResponse
RunnerTraceResponse.description: What came back: status, redacted headers and a redacted, capped body sample.

RunnerTraceRow.title: RunnerTraceRow
RunnerTraceRow.description: One request the runner made, in the shape the probe records it.

ScanProgressOut.title: ScanProgressOut
ScanProgressOut.description:
The volatile scan state, built from the row alone.

``ScanOut`` eager-loads operations, credentials, findings, events and the
token ledger. The one-second progress poll must not pay for any of them, so
this response carries only columns that change while a run is in flight.

authorized.title: Authorized
authorized.description: Must be true to enable a schedule: I own or am authorized to security-test this target.

ScheduleRequest.title: ScheduleRequest
ScheduleRequest.description:
Enable or clear a recurring schedule.

Carries the run's own flags because a schedule *is* a standing run request:
enabling one saves these options for every scheduled run and answers the
same authorization gate. Clearing (``minutes`` null/0) starts nothing, so
``authorized`` defaults to false here rather than being required.

Severity.title: Severity
Severity.description: How bad the weakness is *if real*. Orthogonal to :class:`Confidence`.

SpecReportOut.title: SpecReportOut
SpecReportOut.description: What a spec upload parsed, dropped and complained about.

SpecSkipOut.title: SpecSkipOut
SpecSkipOut.description:
One path item or method the parser dropped, and why.

``method`` is absent when the whole path item was unusable, so the user sees
``/orders — path item is not an object`` rather than a bare path.

SpecUpload.title: SpecUpload
SpecUpload.description: Inline spec content (JSON or YAML text). File upload uses a separate route.

SpecUploadOut.title: SpecUploadOut
SpecUploadOut.description: A spec upload's scan plus its parse report, which the wizard displays.

TargetOwnershipOut.title: TargetOwnershipOut
TargetOwnershipOut.description:
Whether a run of this scan's target will need ownership proof.

Advisory: nothing is fetched from the target to answer it, and the run gate
re-proves ownership live on every run.

TargetPolicy.title: TargetPolicy
TargetPolicy.description:
What the runner must re-establish about the target from its own machine.

The server cleared the target from *its* vantage point; the runner resolves
the name itself, and its resolver (``/etc/hosts``) is the user's. So a target
cleared as private stays private-only, and a verified one must serve the
token from the address the runner pins.
